references.text: The preceding verse where Samson first poses the riddle and describes the terms of the wager, including the thirty linen garments and the thirty sets of clothes.
Samson kills thirty men from Ashkelon and takes their clothes to pay the wager, fulfilling the promise of the thirty sets of clothing.
Joseph gives his brothers changes of clothes, showing that garments were valuable gifts in ancient Israel, just as in the wager.
Naaman brings along changes of clothes as a gift, illustrating the cultural value of garments as currency and presents.
The next verse where Samson actually tells his riddle about the lion and the honey.
